title: How The 'Blue Tsunami' Affects Small And Medium Businesses
summary: See how US midterm election results could affect tariffs, business costs and export orders, and what small and medium businesses can expect over six months.
body_markdown:
Democrats won with promises to bring costs down. If you run a business, you probably have a few questions. Will your next shipment cost less? Will overseas customers start ordering again? And will any of this happen before your next payment is due?


Democrats are projected to control both chambers of Congress from January. They also won Republican-held governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, Texas and Nevada. Trump remains president, so their plans still face negotiations, funding decisions and possible vetoes.[Congressional results](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/democrats-house-control-midterm-election-wins-trump-check-rcna603397) ,[governors’ results](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/democrats-flip-governorships-extending-party-inroads-red-states-rcna607010)


For **small and medium businesses** , the likely direction is more pressure to change **trade policy** , support smaller firms and put conditions on large corporate projects. How much reaches your business by May 2027 will depend on the details.


Photo: CHUTTERSNAP / Unsplash. Illustrative container port in Singapore.


## What has actually flipped


The **US midterm election results** include seven called Senate pickups: Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas. Georgia and Nevada join Iowa, Ohio and Texas in changing governors’ party. A congressional pickup changes representation in Washington; it does not transfer control of a whole state government.[Senate results](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/senate-results)


This guide covers those nine states and 13 additional states with reported House pickups: Arizona, California, Colorado, Indiana, Kentucky, Missouri, Nebraska, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Utah, Virginia and Wisconsin. Election calls reflect reporting checked through 8:30 a.m. Eastern on November 4, pending official certification. Michigan and Minnesota are also covered below because of state legislative changes and newly reported statewide holds. Some races were still uncalled when those results were captured. Redrawn districts also make some comparisons with the previous election less direct.[House calls](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/house-election-results-2026/) ,[race-by-race updates](https://ballotpedia.org/Election_results,_2026)


The six-month outlook below is our assessment of the promises, rather than an announced implementation schedule. It covers Senate seats, governorships, US House pickups and selected state legislative control changes. It does not list every local office or district.


## States with Senate or governor flips


### Texas


James Talarico won the Senate race and Gina Hinojosa won the governorship. House pickups also include Bobby Pulido in the 15th District and Katy Padilla Stout in the 23rd.


Talarico’s[rural plan](https://jamestalarico.com/issue/rural-investment/) calls for removing tariffs on farm equipment, fertilizer and produce that have prompted retaliation. But he also opposes policies expanding competing foreign beef imports. Hinojosa’s[agenda](https://ginafortexas.com/priority/an-affordable-texas-that-works-for-everyone/) targets corporate subsidies and utility costs created by large electricity users.


**For your business:** agricultural-input relief could help purchasing costs, while ranchers may continue seeking protection. Project vendors should check whether changes to incentives affect purchasing schedules. Neither agenda establishes a date for cheaper imports or electricity.


### Iowa


Josh Turek won the Senate seat and Rob Sand won the governorship. Christina Bohannan, Lindsay James and Sarah Trone Garriott also won House seats in districts one, two and three.[Iowa House results](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/iowa-house-results)


Turek opposes unpredictable tariffs but supports strategic protection for industries such as automobiles. Sand wants data centers to cover their own costs, lose tax breaks and face stronger transparency requirements.[Turek’s interview](https://cbs2iowa.com/news/local/beyond-the-podium-josh-turek-discusses-tariffs-healthcare-and-responds-to-gop-criticism) ,[Sand’s plan](https://robsand.com/issues/data-centers/)


**For your business:** expect pressure to reduce disruption to farm trade alongside protection for selected manufacturers. If you sell equipment or materials to data-center projects, confirm the buyer’s budget before buying stock for an expected order.


### Ohio


Sherrod Brown won the Senate race and Amy Acton won the governorship. Brian Poindexter in the seventh House district and Don Leonard in the 15th also won Republican-held seats.


Brown supports targeted tariffs against unfair competition while opposing broad tariffs. Acton proposed a conditional moratorium on data centers unless they meet requirements covering utilities, union labor, environmental standards and community benefits.[Brown’s interview](https://www.news5cleveland.com/news/politics/ohio-politics/as-sherrod-brown-campaigns-across-the-state-for-u-s-senate-he-senses-a-different-tone-in-2026) ,[Acton’s plan](https://actonforgovernor.com/issue/data-centers/)


**For your business:** manufacturers may gain support for domestic production while still paying duties on some inputs. Project vendors could face revised order schedules. Check your product’s tariff treatment and your customer’s project status separately.


### Kansas


Adam Hamilton flipped the Senate seat. Kansas’s outgoing governor, Laura Kelly, is a Democrat; the governor’s office was not a Republican-held seat entering this election.


His[agenda](https://hamiltonforkansas.com/issues/) calls for removing tariffs hurting farmers, expanding export markets, doubling USDA export-promotion funding and requiring congressional approval for new tariffs. He also supports more durable market-access agreements.


**For your business:** this is a clear push to make agricultural trade more reliable. Grain, beef and other agricultural businesses should watch actual agreements and foreign buyers’ responses. Export promotion could help rebuild relationships, but it does not guarantee orders within six months.


### North Carolina


Roy Cooper flipped the Senate seat. Jamie Ager also won the 11th House district.


Cooper’s[cost-reduction plan](https://roycooper.com/roy-cooper-kicks-off-statewide-make-stuff-cost-less-campaign-announces-new-plan-to-lower-food-and-grocery-costs/) promises to stop unpredictable tariffs, support farmers and challenge food-industry mergers and pricing practices that reduce competition.


**For your business:** importers and manufacturers could benefit if relief reaches their goods. Food processors and distributors should also watch competition proposals where a few large companies dominate purchasing or distribution. Legislation or enforcement would have to follow before these promises change your costs or contracts.


### Maine


Troy Jackson defeated Susan Collins for the Senate seat. The governor’s race remained a Democratic hold.


Jackson opposes the trade war with Canada. Collins also opposed Canadian tariffs, so the change is partly about control of Congress rather than a completely new position for this seat.[Candidate statements](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/22/maine-senate-election-trump-tariffs.html)


**For your business:** seafood, wood-products and other businesses with Canadian vendors or customers should watch for reciprocal relief. Benefits depend on the actual goods and transactions covered. Continue checking processing, delivery and payment arrangements while negotiations continue.


### South Carolina


Annie Andrews flipped the Senate seat. The governorship remained Republican.


Her[economic platform](https://drannieandrews.com/issue/an-economy-that-works-for-working-people/) supports trade policies protecting South Carolina’s jobs and farms. She also said a Democratic majority could act against unpredictable tariffs, although her platform gives less detail on individual products.[Direct interview](https://www.wistv.com/2026/10/28/full-interview-annie-andrews-shares-priorities-senate-ahead-election-day/)


**For your business:** there is another Senate vote seeking tariff restraint, but no published product-by-product relief schedule to build into a budget. Importers and manufacturers should wait for that detail before offering customers lower prices.


### Georgia


Keisha Lance Bottoms flipped the governorship. The state’s Senate seat was a Democratic hold.


Her[small-business agenda](https://www.keishaforgovernor.com/issues) proposes a dedicated office, expanded loan and grant programs, and a larger role for smaller firms in state economic-development spending. Her farm agenda supports cooperatives and producers harmed by trade disruption.


**For your business:** watch state budgets for funded programs, qualification rules and application dates. Manufacturers, distributors and agricultural businesses may find new support. A campaign promise does not establish available funding, and a governor cannot independently remove federal tariffs.


### Nevada


Aaron Ford is projected to defeat Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo, adding a fifth Democratic governor pickup. With both legislative chambers already Democratic, this also gives the party control of the governor’s office and legislature.[Governor results](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/democrats-flip-governorships-extending-party-inroads-red-states-rcna607010) ,[state control](https://www.ncsl.org/state-legislatures-news/details/2026-state-legislative-elections-the-results-and-what-they-mean)


Ford’s[economic plan](https://www.fordfornevada.com/issues/economic-development) proposes more small-business financing support, investment in clean energy and battery manufacturing, and faster infrastructure delivery. He also wants to review data-center tax abatements and require those projects to pay their energy and grid costs. His labor agenda includes repealing the state’s right-to-work law and expanding union apprenticeships.


**For your business:** equipment vendors, construction firms and hospitality distributors should watch funded projects and purchasing schedules. Employers should also track labor proposals. None of these promises sets a six-month date for cheaper power, a grant or a new order. Ford’s support for tariff refunds does not establish that your entries qualify or when a refund would arrive.


## Other states with reported House pickups


These changes add votes to Congress. They do not give a representative authority to change state taxes, utility rates or permitting rules alone. House calls come from the election sources above; policy commitments are linked in each section.


### Arizona


JoAnna Mendoza was projected to win the sixth district. This section covers that reported pickup; it makes no call on other Arizona districts.


Mendoza’s[platform](https://www.joannamendoza.com/faq/) opposes disruptive tariffs and supports a long-term Farm Bill, workforce training and energy and water investment. **For owners:** watch agricultural-input relief and training proposals. They could help farm-related and manufacturing businesses, but this win does not create an immediate local program.


### California


Mike McGuire won the first district and Marni von Wilpert won the 48th, both reported Democratic gains. Ami Bera won the redrawn third district and Linda Sánchez won the redrawn 41st; both were already Democratic members of Congress. Those redrawn-seat wins should be distinguished from defeating a Republican incumbent.


[McGuire](https://www.votemikemcguire.com/issues/lowering-costs-for-working-families) and[von Wilpert](https://www.marnivonwilpert.com/issues) support reversing Trump’s tariffs. **For owners:** this adds pressure for import relief. It does not establish new port charges, shipping prices or a common tariff rate for every product.


### Colorado


Manny Rutinel flipped the eighth district. His[agenda](https://www.mannyforcolorado.com/issues) calls for stopping tariffs that raise costs and reducing health and energy expenses.


**For owners:** tariff changes could help businesses buying imported goods and materials. Broader household relief could support demand, but neither effect establishes a confirmed increase in sales. Keep purchasing tied to your actual order book.


### Indiana


J.D. Ford flipped the fifth district. His[platform](https://www.electjdford.com/platform) opposes unpredictable tariffs affecting farms and smaller businesses and calls for data centers to cover their own utility and water costs.


**For owners:** watch proposals affecting farm inputs and manufacturing purchases. Project vendors should check whether funding or oversight measures change buyers’ plans. Ford’s move to Congress does not give him control of Indiana’s state utility policy.


### Kentucky


Zach Dembo flipped the sixth district. His[trade agenda](https://zachdembo.com/priority/end-the-trade-war-and-get-costs-down-for-kentucky-families/) calls for ending the trade war and improving access to markets for farmers and distillers.


**For owners:** exporters have another advocate for reducing barriers. Watch foreign tariffs, buyers’ inventory and new orders together. Removing a barrier can improve your opportunity to sell, while customers may still need time to work through existing stock.


### Missouri


Fred Wellman flipped the second district. His[plan](https://www.wellmanformo.com/affordability) calls for tariff rollback, congressional control over tariff decisions, more housing and stronger conditions on data centers’ power costs.


**For owners:** import costs and project demand are areas to watch. Housing and grid proposals could create opportunities for building-product and equipment vendors if funded. They do not establish a six-month purchasing commitment.


### Nebraska


Denise Powell flipped the second district. Her[platform](https://deniseforcongress.org/priorities/) opposes broad tariffs, supports smaller businesses and workforce training, and calls for better agricultural market access. It also supports targeted agricultural tariffs.


**For owners:** expect a distinction between lowering everyday import costs and protecting domestic farms. Food importers and agricultural exporters could face different outcomes. Read the product coverage before assuming a proposal helps both sides of your business.


### New Jersey


Rebecca Bennett flipped the seventh district. Her[agenda](https://rebeccabennettforcongress.com/priorities/making-new-jersey-more-affordable/) includes housing construction, energy investment, paid family leave and restoring the full state and local tax deduction.


**For owners:** watch actual tax and spending bills before changing your forecast. Housing-related businesses could benefit from funded construction measures. Employer obligations under any leave proposal would depend on its final design.


### New York


Cait Conley flipped the 17th district. Her[platform](https://caitconley.com/policy/) proposes less red tape, more access to capital, workforce training and affordable healthcare to help smaller firms hire. She has also called for reversing harmful tariffs.[Direct interview](https://www.wamc.org/news/2026-11-02/election-2026-ny-17-cait-conley-conversation)


**For owners:** the agenda reaches beyond import costs to staffing and financing access. Programs will need legislation or funding. Continue using current borrowing terms and actual hiring costs until something changes.


### Pennsylvania


Bob Harvie, Bob Brooks, Paige Cognetti and Janelle Stelson won Republican-held seats in the first, seventh, eighth and 10th districts.


Harvie proposed tariff rollback. Cognetti opposed the Canadian trade war. Stelson and Brooks also campaigned against tariffs raising costs.[Harvie’s agenda](https://www.phillyburbs.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/08/11/bob-harvie-policies-congress-new-fair-deal-plan-released-before-midterms-pa-01-2026-elections/91258122007/) ,[Cognetti’s interview](https://www.timesleader.com/news/1763394/election-board-cognetti-makes-her-case-on-health-care-tariffs-and-iran) ,[Stelson’s statements](https://www.cityandstatepa.com/politics/2026/04/janelle-stelson-calls-out-dc-republicans-spiking-gas-prices/412652/) ,[Brooks’s interview](https://keystonenewsroom.com/news/politics/bob-brooks-iran-war-costs/)


**For owners:** the delegation seeking relief is stronger. Steel protection and imported-material costs can still pull in different directions. Assess inputs and finished goods separately.


### Utah


Ben McAdams won the newly drawn first district, which includes Salt Lake City and its suburbs.


In[answers to the Utah Chamber](https://www.utchamber.com/blog/utah-congressional-district-1-candidates-weigh-in-on-issues-important-to-the-business-community/) , McAdams opposed broad tariffs and supported access to capital, simpler permitting, apprenticeships and manufacturing investment. **For owners:** watch for funded changes to financing, project reviews and training. The election itself does not shorten an approval already in progress.


### Virginia


Shannon Taylor flipped the first district and Elaine Luria won back the second. Both campaigned against tariffs. Taylor also supports making data centers cover their costs; Luria called for reversing policies increasing energy costs.[Candidate positions](https://virginiaindependentnews.com/elections/where-the-candidates-in-three-competitive-virginia-us-house-races-stand-on-the-issues/) ,[Taylor’s interview](https://wydaily.com/latest/government/2026/10/26/qa-shannon-taylor-on-corruption-tariffs-and-the-war-in-iran/)


**For owners:** watch import costs, energy proposals and project schedules. If you have federal customers, confirm funded contracts and payment dates before buying for anticipated demand.


### Wisconsin


Mitchell Berman flipped the first district and Rebecca Cooke flipped the third. The governor’s office remained Democratic.


[Berman](https://www.bermanforcongress.com/priorities) wants to remove tariffs on lumber and building materials and make data centers pay their own way. Cooke has called for reversing tariffs damaging agricultural markets.[Cooke’s statements](https://www.news8000.com/news/politics/elections/rebecca-cooke-calls-for-reversing-tariffs-ending-iran-war-during-agricultural-campaign-stops/article_caf65bd3-12ba-4fbd-8631-7217ba48cab4.html)


**For owners:** exporters and building-product businesses have clear proposals to follow. If replacement materials become cheaper, compare their cost with existing inventory before lowering selling prices.


## Statehouse changes and newly reported Democratic holds


### Michigan


Jocelyn Benson won the governor’s race and Abdul El-Sayed won the US Senate race. Both offices stay Democratic. The party also regained the state House and held the state Senate, restoring control of the governor’s office and both legislative chambers. Michigan’s close US House races should be assessed separately; a lead alone is not a pickup.[Michigan results](https://www.mlive.com/politics/2026/11/michigan-democrats-sweep-top-races-5-takeaways-from-the-election.html)


In a[Detroit Economic Club discussion](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2026/09/16/benson-james-discuss-tariffs-taxes-and-business-growth-at-detroit-economic-club-town-hall/) , Benson proposed an agency to make small-business growth easier and a review of the state tax code. She opposed federal tariffs affecting Michigan’s Canadian trade. El-Sayed’s[trade position](https://www.wndu.com/2026/10/21/rogers-el-sayed-outline-differing-approaches-tariffs-ai-during-detroit-economic-club-forum/) supports targeted tariffs tied to an industrial strategy, including support for US electric-vehicle production. His position does not imply removing every import duty.


**For your business:** auto-parts importers and manufacturers should check finished vehicles and production inputs separately. Cross-border distributors should keep using current Canadian and US customs rules. A state government with fewer partisan barriers may advance business-support or tax proposals, but owners still need enacted rules, funding and start dates before changing budgets.


### Minnesota


Amy Klobuchar won the governor’s race, keeping that office Democratic. The DFL, Minnesota’s Democratic Party, also won control of the state House after a tied chamber and retained the state Senate. Individual recounts may affect the size of its majorities.[Minnesota results](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/11/03/control-of-minnesota-capitol-hangs-in-balance-as-voters-decide-all-201-legislative-seats)


Klobuchar campaigned on improving the business climate, cutting red tape and avoiding new tax increases. Legislative leaders have emphasized healthcare affordability, while the next session must write a two-year state budget under financial constraints.[Campaign and transition priorities](https://www.startribune.com/minnesota-legislature-control/601901290)


**For your business:** manufacturers, food businesses and distributors should watch the budget, permitting proposals and healthcare measures. Unified state control may make legislation easier to advance, but it does not establish a new tax break or faster approval for an existing project. Federal tariff policy remains a separate decision.


### More changes in states already covered


**Wisconsin:** Democrats won both legislative chambers, while David Crowley’s governor win kept that office Democratic. That creates a clearer route for state budgets and legislation. Employers and project vendors should watch the actual bills and purchasing plans.[Wisconsin legislative results](https://www.wpr.org/news/wisconsin-assembly-senate-election-results-2026)


**Georgia and North Carolina:** NCSL reports Democratic gains in control of both states’ Houses. These are state legislative changes, separate from the congressional races discussed above. A governor’s proposal still needs the relevant legislative votes and funding, including support in the other chamber.[Statehouse results](https://www.ncsl.org/state-legislatures-news/details/2026-state-legislative-elections-the-results-and-what-they-mean)


**Pennsylvania:** Democrats claimed control of the state Senate, but the reporting checked still noted outstanding race calls. Gov. Josh Shapiro and legislative leaders have proposed a higher minimum wage, more housing and transit funding. Businesses should monitor payroll proposals and funded construction opportunities while treating final chamber control as provisional.[Pennsylvania reporting](https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2026/11/pennsylvania-house-election-results-legislature-control-elections/)


**Still pending:** the sources reviewed had not established final control of Arizona’s Senate or Texas’s House. Alaska and Mississippi’s US Senate races also remained uncalled in NBC’s 8:21 a.m. Eastern update. Those leads are not included as additional pickups.[Statehouse update](https://www.ncsl.org/state-legislatures-news/details/2026-state-legislative-elections-the-results-and-what-they-mean) ,[Senate update](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/senate-results)


## What can realistically happen by May 2027


### November and December


Expect transition plans and negotiations. Price orders using current duties and operating costs. Review[vendor contracts and payment terms](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/vendor-contracts-and-payment-terms) , especially where prices or delivery schedules can change.


### January through March


The incoming Congress can set hearings, introduce bills and negotiate changes. New governors can propose budgets and use powers available under state law. Tariff repeal, grants and changes to employer rules each have different legal and funding requirements.


### March through May


Our expectation is that selective relief is more plausible than every promise becoming law. Agricultural inputs, Canadian trade and congressional oversight are areas to watch. Larger tax, healthcare and workforce measures may take longer. A bill introduced in January could still be under negotiation in May.


### By the numbers


The proposed Trade Review Act would generally limit presidential tariffs to **60 days** without enacted congressional approval. Antidumping and countervailing duties are excluded. It remains a proposal and would need renewed action in the next Congress. Ordinary Senate legislation usually requires **60 votes** to end debate under current rules; some expedited procedures use different rules. Overriding a presidential veto requires two-thirds support in each chamber.[Bill summary](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1272) ,[Senate procedures](https://www.senate.gov/about/powers-procedures/voting.htm) ,[veto process](https://www.senate.gov/about/origins-foundations/senate-and-constitution/constitution.htm)


These hurdles help explain why a majority creates an opportunity for change without guaranteeing a date for savings.


## What this means for your next order


For importers, relief needs to cover the actual product, origin and entry date. Ask your customs broker to confirm those details before changing a quote.


For exporters, a lower US tariff does not remove another country’s restrictions. Confirm demand and payment terms before increasing production.


For domestic businesses, watch funding, qualification rules and application dates. A proposed loan program or incentive belongs on your watchlist until it is available to your business.


The **US midterm election results** could also create a difficult inventory transition. New stock may become cheaper while older goods still carry higher costs. A stronger order book can require more cash even when each unit costs less to buy.


## Keep purchasing and cash flow aligned


Put vendor payments, import costs, expected delivery and customer collections on the same calendar. Test what happens if relief arrives late or a buyer pays later than expected.

A[Line of Credit](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/line-of-credit) can support recurring working-capital needs. Approval and applicable requirements apply.

Use confirmed demand, current costs and realistic collection dates to decide what to buy. Adjust the plan when a policy change applies to your business.


## Frequently asked questions


### Does a flipped state mean all its business rules change?


A House or Senate pickup changes representation in Congress. State taxes, programs and regulations depend on the relevant state authorities and laws.


### Will tariffs fall within six months?


Selective relief is possible, but no universal timetable follows from the election. Keep using current duties until an effective measure covers your goods.


### Should I wait to place an order?


Compare the cost of waiting with confirmed sales and delivery commitments. A possible saving may be smaller than the cost of missing a customer order.


### Will the result lower my borrowing costs?


There is no automatic reduction in borrowing costs. Your lender’s terms, your business’s credit profile and broader financial conditions still matter.
